headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap in Replit Agent; pairwise leakage and conflict are plausible, while Risingwave adds no documented mitigation surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Replit Agent reads and writes Repl workspace files and can execute shell commands, so malicious content in shared files could steer it. Risingwave is open-source but has no documented interactive bridge to the agent, so the pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly evidenced. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace files
IF file contents are treated as instructions by Replit Agent
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Add a manual review step before acting on file-derived instructions
Use allowlisted command templates only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file-originated content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration and has broad network egress, so sensitive data can leave the workspace. Risingwave itself has no documented egress, but the pair still creates a leakage path through the agent side. Because the interaction is not directly documented, medium is the higher defensible severity.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment configuration are present in the Repl workspace
IF Replit Agent transmits those contents to external services
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace
Rotate any exposed API keys
Restrict outbound network destinations
Store sensitive config in a separate secret manager
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data classification controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shells in a persistent Repl filesystem shared across sessions. Risingwave is a data-engineering system with no documented locking or coordination surface here, so concurrent writes to the same repo or workspace can collide. Defaults are dangerous because state changes can overwrite each other.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same repository or workspace
IF no external lock or merge gate is enforced
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Require git branch isolation
Add a manual merge review step
requires-engineering: implement workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Replit Agent can generate code and modify files, and Risingwave is a downstream data-engineering system that could consume those outputs. There is no documented verification boundary between them, so A's output may become B's input without checks. The blast radius is multiple work products rather than immediate irreversible harm, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Risingwave ingests artifacts produced by Replit Agent
IF no validation or review step checks those artifacts before use
mitigations: Add checksum or schema validation
Require human approval before ingestion
Compare outputs against a known-good baseline
Log provenance for generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly touches secrets and deployment configuration, while Risingwave is an open-source data system with no documented residency or retention controls in the profile. That mismatch can create compliance gaps if regulated data is placed in the Repl workspace. The other agent is not cited for a specific residency rule because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are stored in the Repl workspace
IF retention or residency requirements apply to that data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Document a data-handling policy for the pair
Minimize secrets in prompts and files
Review retention settings before use
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
